title: Multigrain Bread, Reduced Calorie and/or High Fiber

content.title: About
content.content: Multigrain bread with reduced calories and high fiber is made from a blend of whole grains, bran, and seeds. It has a dense texture, a light nutty aroma, and is suitable for diet-conscious eating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The bread contains at least five different grain types, boosting its nutritional profile.
Calorie reduction is achieved by using high‑fiber whole‑grain flour and limiting added sugars and fats.
Fiber slows carbohydrate absorption, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.
Athletes often use this bread for post‑workout recovery due to its balanced macronutrients.
Gluten‑free versions are available by substituting wheat with alternative grains.

items.title: High Fiber Content
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate cholesterol levels.

items.title: Reduced Calorie Count
items.content: Lower calories make the bread suitable for weight‑management diets without sacrificing volume.

items.title: Rich in B‑Vitamins
items.content: The grain blend provides thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals: Magnesium and Iron
items.content: These minerals are important for muscle function and oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Low Glycemic Index
items.content: Compared with white bread, it has a lower GI, aiding blood‑glucose control.

items.title: Grain Allergies
items.content: People allergic to wheat or other grains may experience reactions.

items.title: Gluten Content
items.content: The standard version contains gluten and is not suitable for celiac disease.

items.title: Excessive Fiber Intake
items.content: Too much fiber can cause bloating and gastrointestinal discomfort.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use the bread as a base for sandwiches, toast, serve with avocado or low‑fat cheese, or as a side to soups. For extra flavor, toast slices until golden.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bread in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature before use.
